html:
Al-Farabi was a philosopher and music theorist of the early Islamic world, called the "Second Teacher", second only to Aristotle, the First. He was born around 870, probably at Farab (Otrar) on the Syr Darya in today's Kazakhstan, though some place his birth in Afghanistan.

He spent most of his working life in Baghdad, the capital of the Abbasid caliphs, and his last years in Aleppo and Damascus, where he died in 950. He wrote in Arabic.

  • He wrote commentaries on Aristotle's logic and made logic central to Islamic philosophy.
  • His Virtuous City, inspired by Plato's Republic, describes the ideal state, ruled by a philosopher, and the kinds of bad states.
  • His Great Book of Music explained the theory of sound, scales and instruments.
  • He tried to show that philosophy and religion, rightly understood, agree.

He was the first to present philosophy as a whole system in the Islamic world. Avicenna said he only understood Aristotle's Metaphysics after reading al-Farabi, and he influenced Averroes and Maimonides. Kazakhstan honours him as a national figure, and his face is on its banknotes.
